nodes.name: EL NINO JARVIS Cyberpunk.html
nodes.summary: Prototype or design mockup of the JARVIS UI in a cyberpunk visual style, containing a full self-contained HTML/CSS/JS dashboard intended as a reference or source design for the JARVIS graph-intelligence interface.

nodes.name: OPUS_CONTEXT_DUMP.md
nodes.summary: Comprehensive project context dump capturing the Mr. Ripley / El Niño system architecture, epoch roadmap, current implementation status, La Niña architecture specification, scorecard schema, and dashboard design requirements — intended to provide an LLM with full project context for dashboard generation.
nodes.languageNotes: Written primarily in Hungarian with embedded English technical terminology; contains 32 sections covering system architecture, roadmap epochs E1-E6, and La Niña governance specification.

nodes.name: el_nino_jarvis_interface (6).html
nodes.summary: Version 6 of the JARVIS interface prototype HTML file, representing an iterative design artifact for the El Niño JARVIS dashboard UI prior to the React/Vite production implementation.
nodes.languageNotes: The '(6)' in the filename indicates this is at least the sixth iteration of the interface prototype, typical of design-by-iteration workflows.

nodes.name: el_nino_project_plan_v1.md
nodes.summary: Master planning document for the El Niño Layer-3 decision engine project, covering the six-epoch roadmap (E1-E6), Slice 2 fit assessment, La Niña architecture with the 19-point problem inventory, backtesting and paper trading strategy, human-approved policy evolution process, and key terminology — the authoritative strategic blueprint for the entire system.
nodes.languageNotes: Bilingual document mixing Hungarian section headers with English technical content; 56 sections spanning 596 lines covering strategic planning, architecture decisions, and epoch-by-epoch implementation guidance.

nodes.name: sarkallatos_pontok.md
nodes.summary: Concise summary of key open questions and agreed negotiation points for the El Niño / La Niña system, covering La Niña monitor architecture, backtest and paper trading decisions, data collection and learning strategy, and look-ahead bias handling.
nodes.languageNotes: Written entirely in Hungarian ('sarkallatos pontok' means 'cardinal/pivotal points'); acts as a decision-tracking artifact complementing the larger project plan.
